findings.note: Listed among the additional (non-primary) sponsors of HB 1074, Constitutional Amendment/Citizens-Only Voting, which proposes a constitutional amendment that only a citizen of the United States who is 18 or older and otherwise qualified may vote. The bill was filed May 23, 2024 per the bill text, passed the Senate third reading 40-4 on 2024-06-27 and was chaptered as S.L. 2024-18 on 2024-06-28. Her own floor vote was not read.
NC House, Third Reading (roll call #810), 2024-12-11: yea (tally 73–45); census gate: none.
subjects: photo ID for all voters (constitutional amendment, in person and by mail)

findings.motion: Second Reading, Election Law Changes (House vote 66 Ayes, 47 Noes)
findings.note: Member vote list shows Aye on second reading of HB 958, Election Law Changes. The ratified text adds a rule that a county board processes a registration application only if the applicant affirmatively says they are a U.S. citizen, with a sworn citizenship form for blank answers, and orders a process to remove voters flagged as non-citizens by a federal database. Bill page shows the Governor vetoed it on 2026-08-17.
subjects: voter-roll checks against federal citizenship data

findings.motion: M11 Concur, Election Law Changes (House vote 62 Ayes, 47 Noes)
findings.note: Member vote list shows Aye on the House vote to concur in the Senate changes to HB 958, Election Law Changes. Same bill content as above: citizenship answer required on registration forms and a removal process for voters flagged by a federal database.
subjects: voter-roll checks against federal citizenship data
